A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepMath-103K dataset and research work. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 has no appendices; v2's Appendices A–E were included, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, SFT and RL benchmark results in Table 3, and reasoning-length and cognitive-behavior analyses in Figures 7–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds model and benchmark results, dataset uniqueness analyses, and a contamination audit in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction stages, difficulty filtering, and multi-solution answer-consistency procedure are retained. v2 newly specifies GRPO with DAPO fixes and tests additional starting checkpoints, without establishing an algorithmic revision. Omission of v1's judge-order-swapping description does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the English subset of PolyMath and on GPQA-Diamond, extending coverage beyond the original six mathematical benchmarks to biology, physics, and chemistry. GPQA appeared in v1's decontamination process, but science reasoning performance was not evaluated there.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Qwen-2.5-Math-7B and its SRL-Zoo comparator, Oat-Zero-7B (spelled Qat in the tables), Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, OpenMath-Nemotron-1.5B, and o1-mini/o3-mini reference scores. Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct is removed. Figure 1a adds STILL-3-RL to the difficulty comparison; DSR-Preview is a shortened name for the retained DeepScaleR-Preview dataset.

E3.justification: The experimental design expands to training from Qwen-2.5-Math-7B and OpenMath-Nemotron-1.5B with separate configurations. New analyses introduce embedding-similarity greater than 0.98 for identifying overlap and normalized indel similarity above 90% for contamination detection. Pass@1 with 16 samples is retained; newly disclosed decoding settings do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-dataset uniqueness and t-SNE analyses (Figures 5–6), a MATH500 contamination audit (Appendix A), and response-length tracking during training (Figure 9a). The one-versus-three-solution SFT comparison is retained in Appendix B. Table 1 drops the MATH500 contamination example.

E5.justification: Both versions report pass@1 using 16 samples and average six GPT-4o difficulty ratings per problem. Neither provides training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Relabeling cognitive-behavior 'variance' as frequency change clarifies an existing quantity rather than changing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results include DeepMath-Omn-1.5B scoring 64.0/57.3 on AIME24/25 and DeepMath-Zero-7B scoring 41.7 overall on GPQA-Diamond. DeepMath-1.5B's reported MATH500/AIME24 scores change from 89.0/39.8 to 89.9/37.3; v1 lacks sufficient settings to establish a same-condition comparison. Original DeepMath-Zero-7B and SFT mathematics rows remain unchanged. v2 also introduces an inconsistency: Figure 1b gives SRL-Zoo 8.5 on AIME25 while Table 3 retains 8.7.

T1.justification: No formal theoretical contribution, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised. Mathematical examples in Figure 2 and Table 2 are retained. The new similarity thresholds specify empirical analysis procedures.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes a challenging, decontaminated, verifiable dataset that improves mathematical reasoning. v2 adds explicit claims of substantial uniqueness relative to other datasets and demonstrated generalization to biology, physics, and chemistry. It also extends performance-superiority claims to additional model variants and comparisons with o1-mini and o3-mini.

C2.justification: v2 attributes science-task generalization to forum-derived diversity and rigorous curation, and interprets growing response lengths and cognitive behaviors as reproducing an 'aha moment.' Appendix E newly acknowledges difficulty-rating bias, topical imbalance, and guessable answers. v1's explicit caution that solution length does not directly measure quality is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds the verl framework, GRPO/DAPO and reward details, model-specific hyperparameters and training budgets (Appendix C), decoding settings, asset licenses, a direct dataset link, and a stated code/model-weight release. It clarifies the Math StackExchange source subsets. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit description of swapping question order during decontamination judgments.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces broad coverage of chain-of-thought methods, inference scaling, and reasoning efficiency with a dataset taxonomy spanning continued pretraining, SFT, and RL. Added works include OpenWebMath, MathPile, InfiMM-WebMath, MegaMath, and OpenMathReasoning. The introduction newly emphasizes forum-derived problem novelty relative to datasets that reuse common competition sources.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Section 4 becomes 'DeepMath Series Models' with separate setup, mathematics, generalization, and analysis subsections. SFT results move to Appendix B, other appendices are introduced, and the extended discussion of possible training applications is condensed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned; new uniqueness, embedding, and contamination displays and several tables are added. Table 3 expands, with SFT rows moved to Table 5. Earlier reasoning plots are combined in Figure 9, replacing benchmark-specific lengths with aggregate bars and shortening the cognitive plot to 500 steps. Figure 9 introduces an incorrect caption describing difficulty and AIME25 instead of its actual panels.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited reproducibility information and empirical scope: Section 4.1 and Appendix C supply missing configurations, while additional checkpoints, science evaluations, and overlap audits make the dataset's usefulness and distinctiveness more assessable. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including Figure 9's incorrect caption and the overbroad claim that DeepMath-Omn-1.5B leads every benchmark, contradicted by its Minerva score of 28.3 versus DeepScaleR's 42.2 in Table 3.
